Rishi Kumar Gupta And 2 Others vs Union Of India And Others
on 11 November, 2024
Author: Manoj Kumar Gupta

Bench: Manoj Kumar Gupta
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?In The High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

sentences.text:
Petitioner :- Rishi Kumar Gupta And 2 Others
Respondent :- Union Of India And Others

Counsel for Petitioner :- Nanda Kumar Shukla,Pranav Kumar Tripathi
Counsel for Respondent :- A.S.G.I.,C.S.C.,Mahendra Pratap,Surendra Prasad Yadav,Vaibhav 
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Gupta,J.
Hon'ble Anish Kumar Gupta,J.
1.

The instant petition has been filed praying for a direction to the competent authority to pay
compensation to the petitioners in terms of award dated 07.12.2016 passed by Special Land
Acquisition Offier, Gorakhpur along with interest in respect of the acquired land of the petitioners
bearing Arazi No. 3400 area 0.299 hectare.

2.  It is not disputed that the aforesaid land of the petitioners was acquired by National Highway Authority of India (in short the 'N.H.A.I.') under the provisions of National Highways Act, 1956 (in short the 'Act 1956').
An award was declared on 07.12.2016 by the competent authority fixing compensation at the rate of Rs.5,000/- per square meter.

The same was challenged by the N.H.A.I.
before the Arbitrator/District Magistrate under Section 3G(5) of the Act 1956.

The Arbitrator passed Rishi Kumar Gupta And 2 Others vs Union Of India And Others on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80095322/
1 an award on 03.01.2018 and directed the Special Land Acquisition Officer to pass a fresh award in pursuance of joint inspection report dated 23.12.2017.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thereafter the competent authority passed a fresh award on 13.02.2018 treating the aforesaid land of the petitioners as agricultural instead of residential.

The award dated 13.02.2018 was challenged before the Arbitrator by the affected persons and the Arbitrator declared the amended award dated 13.02.2018 as null and void and affirmed the original award dated 07.12.2016.
It was challenged by N.H.A.I. under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
The District Judge decided the challenge vide order dated 15.03.2024 and rejected the same.
In between, N.H.A.I. filed an application under Section 33 for correction of the award.

It was allowed by order dated 03.04.2018 and the previous award of the Arbitrator dated 03.01.2018 was recalled and as a result, the subsequent award of the Competent Authority was declared as null and void.

The matter is now pending in appeal under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 being Defective No. 227 of 2024 and wherein the issue as to whether the Arbitrator could have recalled the order of remand dated 03.01.2018, is also to be considered.

In the aforesaid background, we passed the following order dated 25.09.2024:
"1.

There is a dispute as to whether the acquired land is agricultural or residential and it is submitted that the said issue is under consideration in appeal filed by NHAI under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 bearing Defective No.
227 of 2024.
2. As per award of Competent Authority dated 13.02.2018 where-under the acquired land was treated as agricultural, the circle rate at the relevant time was held to be Rs.85,00,000/- per hectare.
The said award has been declared to be void by the Arbitrator as it was passed in pursuance of remand order dated 03.01.2018, which itself was recalled by him by order dated 02.11.2018.
The issue in appeal is also whether the Arbitrator could have recalled the order of remand dated 03.01.2018.

3. It is not in dispute that the NHAI itself contends that the land is agricultural and even if, it is treated to be so, at least the amount determined by the Competent Authority under award dated 13.02.2018 would be payable to the land owners.

4. Shri Surendra Prasad Yadav, learned counsel appearing for NHAI states that NHAI is ready to release payment to the Competent Authority for disbursal of compensation amount to the petitioners in terms of the calculation made under award dated 13.02.2018 within three weeks.

5. Accordingly, we hereby direct that the payment of compensation to the petitioners be made at agricultural rate as per award dated 13.02.2018 without prejudice to the rights and contentions of the parties in Appeal under Section 37 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 Defective No. 227 of 2024 pending in this Court, as otherwise the petitioners, whose land had been acquired long back and have not been paid a single penny as compensation so far, would be at great loss and the acquisition itself would in that event be rendered illegal.
Rishi Kumar Gupta And 2 Others vs Union Of India And Others on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80095322/
2 6.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: List as fresh on 24 October 2024.

7. The General Manager, NHAI will file his personal affidavit and apprise the Court as to whether payment in terms of the aforesaid award of the Competent Authority dated 13.02.2018 treating the land to be agricultural has been made and what amount has been paid to the petitioners."

3. In compliance of the said order, the Project Director, N.H.A.I. Gorakhpur has filed an affidavit in which the stand taken is that the petitioners were issued repeated notices and they were also informed over their mobile numbers to come and furnish the requisite details so that compensation amount is disbursed in their favour but they did not turn up and consequently, the compensation amount could not be released in their favour.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that in all the notices issued by the authorities, the exact amount which they intend to pay to the petitioners has not been disclosed.

5. Having regard to the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, we directed the instant matter to be put up after lunch at 2:00 P.M.
6.

Sri Rajeev Gupta, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel was requested to obtain instructions from the competent authority with regard to the amount, which would be released in favour of the petitioners.
He has placed before us Form No.11, according to which Rs. 1,09,52,263.51 would be paid to the petitioners in case the compensation is calculated as per the award dated 13.02.2018.
He submits that the amounts have been calculated as on the date of award on 13.02.2018, as it includes interest at the rate of 12% per annum till the date of award i.e. 13.02.2018.

7. Sri Rajeev Gupta, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel appearing for the competent authority and Sri S.P. Yadav, learned counsel appearing for N.H.A.I. states that interest for the subsequent period until the date of payment would also be released in favour of the petitioners subject to the final outcome of the pending appeal and without prejudice to the rights and contentions of the petitioners as well as N.H.A.I. in the said proceeding.

8. In our opinion since admittedly the land of the petitioners has been acquired and they have not been paid a single penny towards compensation so far and it is not disputed by N.H.A.I. that compensation at least by treating the land as agricultural is to be paid to the petitioners and therefore, we are of the opinion that payment of compensation as per computation done above would subserve the ends of justice at this stage.

9. Accordingly, we dispose of the instant petition with a direction to the N.H.A.I. and the competent authority to ensure that the compensation amount as noted along with interest of 12% per annum from the date of award until the date of actual payment shall be released in favour of the petitioners within three weeks from today.
